name: datagoblin_legal
description: Indian legal documents: central statutes, the Constitution, and reported judgments, with every value tied to a locatable quote.

fields.name: document_title
fields.description: The document's own title, e.g. 'Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar' or 'BNS s. 3 - General explanations'.

fields.name: document_type
fields.description: One of statute, judgment, constitution or fee_schedule.

fields.name: citation
fields.description: The reporter or act citation printed for the document.

fields.name: court
fields.description: The court that decided the judgment, empty for legislation.

fields.name: jurisdiction
fields.description: The state or union jurisdiction the document belongs to (India for central law and the Supreme Court).

fields.name: tier
fields.description: Which tier of law the document sits in: local (this edition's own state), regional (another state), or national (union law).

fields.name: year
fields.description: The year of enactment, publication or judgment.

fields.name: act
fields.description: The Act, Code or Constitution the document belongs to.

fields.name: section
fields.description: The section, article or order rule the document covers, when it covers one.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: A verbatim excerpt from the document body, not a paraphrase.

fields.name: dlsa_eligible
fields.description: True only where the document states eligibility for free legal aid; never written false.

validation_rules: Every stored value carries a quote that resolves against the stored document text.
A judgment's court and jurisdiction come from the document, not from its filename.
dlsa_eligible is written true only where a quote states eligibility; there is no false value.
planner_guidance: A row is one legal document: a section of an Act, a constitutional article, or a reported judgment. Prefer official court and India Code sources. Record the document's own title and citation; do not invent a reporter citation. Documents fall into three tiers: local law of a single state (Delhi statutes and the state legal aid authority), regional decisions of a state High Court, and national law (central statutes, the Constitution, the Supreme Court). A document can sit in more than one tier.
extractor_guidance: Quote the exact words of the document. A summary is a verbatim excerpt, never a paraphrase. Leave a field absent rather than guessing it.
examples: What does BNS section 3 say about general explanations?
Which Supreme Court judgments require a magistrate to consider legal aid before remand?
Show Delhi High Court judgments about legal aid in criminal cases.
